segments.text: "Welcome to today's edition of Robotics Roundup, your daily dose of innovation and insight from the world of robotics.
I'm your host, [name], and on August 1st, 2026, we're covering some exciting developments in the industry.
DroneDeploy is being acquired for a whopping $845 million, while Procore Technologies gets to leverage its new ROS toolset.
Meanwhile, Atlas Energy is preparing to launch a Kodiak-powered autonomous truck fleet with 100 vehicles by 2027 - it's going to be an interesting year."
From The Robot Report, "Procore Technologies acquires DroneDeploy for $845M".
Procore Technologies has acquired DroneDeploy, a robotics and visual intelligence platform provider, in an all-cash deal worth approximately $845 million.
This acquisition aims to accelerate Procore's AI strategy by developing digital co-workers that can track project progress, make sense of it, and take action.
DroneDeploy offers automated inspections on over 3 million job sites across more than 180 countries, utilizing its platform to enhance project management capabilities.
The acquisition strengthens Procore's position in the construction industry, where AI-powered solutions are increasingly sought after.
As a result, Procore can now integrate its own technology with DroneDeploy's robotics and visual intelligence capabilities, driving innovation in project management.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: A new tool to create ros2 package with executables, C++ and Python node in one package."
This story is about a new utility script named ros2_pkg_create.py that generates ROS 2 package templates supporting both C++ and Python nodes within a single package.

The tool was developed to simplify the process of creating ROS 2 packages for developers, allowing them to easily generate necessary files for compilation, installation, and testing of code in a single package.
By downloading the script and running it with a package name, users can create a complete ROS 2 package with C++ and Python nodes, executables, and other required files.
This new tool aims to streamline the development process for developers working on ROS 2 projects.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Atlas Energy to expand Kodiak-powered autonomous truck fleet to 100 vehicles by 2027."
Atlas Energy Solutions is expanding its autonomous truck fleet with Kodiak AI's physical AI-powered technology, aiming to reach 100 vehicles by mid-2027.
The company has added a second simultaneous load-out point along its 42-mile Dune Express sand conveyor system, increasing the reach of autonomous deliveries and responsiveness to customer demand.
This upgrade enables faster loading and unloading of materials, optimizing the entire production process.
Atlas Energy expects to have its fleet operating on public roads in early 2027, dramatically expanding its reach.
The expansion is expected to further solidify Kodiak AI's position in the autonomous truck market.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: VectorField Planner: 7 µs global path queries with strict optimality — REST API for occupancy grids, Nav2 plugin on roadmap."
The VectorField Planner has achieved a significant milestone, providing a fast and efficient solution for warehouse and fleet deployments.
This system solves a complex goal, such as finding a charging station or pick station, and returns a strictly optimal path in microseconds for any start cell query without re-searching the map.
The planner measures 1M-cell 3D warehouses maps with peak memory of 5MB and can handle up to 10,000 simultaneous queries.
A native Nav2 global-planner plugin is currently on the roadmap for further integration and expansion.
This breakthrough marks a significant advancement in artificial intelligence and navigation technology.
From The Robot Report, "FCC robot ruling shines a spotlight on U.S. policy; how next-gen AI can help warehousing."
The Federal Communications Commission has imposed limits on the imports of new humanoid and mobile robots in the United States, highlighting the need for clearer regulations in robotics.
A recent statement from Derik Pridmore, co-founder and CEO of OSARO, underscores the significance of adaptable AI-driven automation in evolving warehouse robotics.

Pridmore emphasizes the importance of hardware-agnostic design, continuous learning, and real-world monitoring over flashy demos, as he notes that these advancements have enabled robots to transition from limited perception systems to more sophisticated and effective operations.
By adopting this approach, warehouse robotics can benefit significantly from next-gen AI capabilities.
From The Robot Report, "KUKA deploys Automation Management Platform for North American automakers".

KUKA has successfully deployed its Automation Management Platform (AMP) at its Toledo Production Operations in Ohio, a major automotive manufacturing facility that produces over 300 vehicle bodies per day.

AMP combines industrial automation and AI-driven decision-making to increase operational flexibility and enhance productivity by providing an open orchestration solution for connecting existing automation infrastructure with next-generation AI-powered technologies.

The platform was deployed after a thorough analysis of the facility's current systems, allowing KUKA to modernize and drive higher efficiency through more comprehensive automation without replacing existing assets.
This deployment marks a significant milestone in KUKA's efforts to support North American automakers in their transition to Industry 4.0.
"DroneDeploy just took off - and we're grounded!
Thanks for tuning in to today's robotic rundown, where the latest acquisition is the buzz of the day - Procore's swoop to DroneDeploy.
Until tomorrow's circuit breakers, robot enthusiasts, keep on charging!"
